import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 314

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/


namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture314

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]

/-- The size of a largest induced path of $G$, as a natural number.

A subset $s \subseteq V(G)$ is an *induced path* when the induced subgraph
`G.induce s` is a tree in which every vertex has degree at most $2$
(equivalently: a tree that is itself a path graph). We define
`largestInducedPathSize G` as the supremum of `s.card` over all such subsets.

**Disambiguation.** This is *not* the `SimpleGraph.path` invariant, which is the
floor of the average distance — that one is the wrong tool for WOWII Conjecture
314, where $\mathrm{path}(G)$ denotes the **size of a largest induced path**.

TODO: it would probably be clearer to rename the `SimpleGraph.path` invariant to
something like `pathBound` / `floorAvgDist` to avoid this naming collision. -/
noncomputable def largestInducedPathSize (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : ℕ :=
  sSup { n | ∃ s : Finset α,
              s.card = n ∧
              (G.induce (s : Set α)).IsTree ∧
              ∀ v : (s : Set α), (G.induce (s : Set α)).degree v ≤ 2 }

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 314](http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html#conj314):

For every finite simple connected graph $G$ with $n > 1$ vertices,
if $G$ is triangle-free and $\mathrm{path}(G) \le 4$, then $G$ is well totally
dominated.

Here $\mathrm{path}(G) = \mathrm{largestInducedPathSize}\, G$ is the **size of a
largest induced path** in $G$, defined locally above.

**Disambiguation.** Earlier revisions of this file used the `SimpleGraph.path`
invariant, but that is the *floor of the average distance*, not the size of a
largest induced path — a different quantity that makes Conjecture 314 vacuous
in many cases.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture314 [Nontrivial α] (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hG : G.Connected)
    (hTriFree : ∀ a b c : α, G.Adj a b → G.Adj b c → G.Adj c a → False)
    (hPath : largestInducedPathSize G ≤ 4) :
    IsWellTotallyDominated G := by
  sorry

-- Sanity checks

/-- The complete graph $K_3$ has a triangle. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example : ∃ a b c : Fin 3, (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)).Adj a b ∧
    (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)).Adj b c ∧ (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)).Adj c a := by
  exact ⟨0, 1, 2, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩

/-- `largestInducedPathSize G` is nonneg. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) [DecidableRel G.Adj] :
    0 ≤ largestInducedPathSize G := Nat.zero_le _

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture314

findings.description: The disambiguation paragraphs at lines 40–45 and 62–65 incorrectly say that the current `SimpleGraph.path` is the floor of average distance and differs from `largestInducedPathSize`. At the reviewed commit, `FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/VertexDistance.lean`, lines 45–54, defines `SimpleGraph.path` as the maximum number of vertices in an induced path. On finite graphs this agrees with the local tree-and-degree definition. The mathematical definition and conjecture are faithful; the warning and proposed `floorAvgDist` rename are outdated.
findings.source_evidence: WOWII definition 35 states: “The number of vertices of a largest induced path of the graph” (https://web.archive.org/web/20260723161735id_/http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/wowIIdefs.js). The current shared Lean definition implements precisely this invariant, as confirmed by its source and `#print SimpleGraph.path`.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove or update both disambiguation paragraphs and the associated rename suggestion. Describe the current shared invariant as an equivalent finite-graph formulation. No change to the conjecture's mathematical statement is needed.

reformulations.difference: The source takes the maximum vertex count of an induced path. Lean takes a natural-number supremum of vertex counts of induced subgraphs that are trees with every degree at most two.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A finite nonempty tree of maximum degree at most two is a path: starting at a leaf and following successive unused neighbors cannot repeat vertices, and connectedness prevents any vertices being left outside this maximal path. Conversely, every nonempty path is such a tree. Candidate cardinalities are bounded by the number of vertices, so their natural-number supremum is their maximum. On the empty graph the definition returns zero. Boundedness and equality with a computable finite maximum were proved in the scratch file; the full tree/path characterization was checked mathematically, not formalized there.

reformulations.difference: The source defines well total domination by saying every inclusion-minimal total dominating set is minimum. The imported Lean predicate instead says all inclusion-minimal total dominating sets have equal cardinality.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every finite total dominating set T contains an inclusion-minimal total dominating subset U. If all minimal sets have equal cardinality, any minimal S satisfies |S| = |U| ≤ |T|, hence is minimum. Conversely, two minimum sets have equal cardinality. This equivalence was proved as `Review314.well_total_iff_minimal_is_minimum`. A separate Lean proof shows that connectedness and nontriviality ensure existence of a minimal total dominating set, excluding vacuity in the conjecture's domain.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found in the definition, conjecture, or either sanity-check example. The archived source marks Conjecture 314 open, agreeing with the category; the live servers timed out, so no newer live status was verified. `/workspace/review/scratch.lean` compiles successfully. Tests cover empty and singleton graphs, paths through six vertices, complete and edgeless graphs, and cycles C3–C6. In particular, K2 and C5 satisfy the hypotheses and conclusion; P5 has minimal total dominating sets of sizes three and four but is correctly excluded because its path number is five. The main verification lemmas have no `sorry` dependencies. The reviewed mathematical files match the specified commit; pre-existing sandbox scaffolding was left untouched.
